correctness.rationale: Exact monodromy and its two positive multipliers follow from trace/determinant and positive-definite similarity. For each fixed duty, the weighted-power-mean ordering makes coefficients of the entire stability-deficit series change sign at most once; after division by the first positive power the resulting function is strictly increasing and crosses zero once precisely when the mean matrix is Hurwitz. The angular and duty cuts are strict equivalent inequalities, including orthogonal and equal-dwell edges. Differentiation and elementary hyperbolic asymptotics prove the logarithmic and square-root edge laws with nonzero constants. 525 independently calculated matrix-exponential spectral radii agree with the exact formula; these finite checks are illustrative and not proof.

originality.rationale: The full accessible text of the March 2026 switched mechanical-oscillator article and specific claims/equations of prior mathematical papers were compared at the level of matrix class and theorem implication. The mechanical model has companion-form matrices with common upper row and forbids stabilization of two saddles in that restricted class; the present two rotated symmetric saddles are outside it, and its exact angle–period–duty boundary is not a corollary of the mechanical exclusion. General Floquet/eigenvalue criteria, fast-switching sufficiency and qualitative matrix-product monotonicity are acknowledged as prior art; no monopoly is asserted on them. A 2021 cooperative stable-mode calculation has different mode spectra and normalization. No checked source or recovered prior finding gives the complete derived joint boundary or square-root/logarithmic edge laws. The historical-priority caveat for inaccessible full texts remains real.

value.rationale: The natural minimal design problem asks exactly how unstable eigendirections, duty imbalance and switching period jointly permit stabilization, not just whether fast switching can work. The derived necessary-and-sufficient region, unique period cutoff for every fixed duty, sharp angle threshold, exact tolerance window and singular orthogonal/critical edge laws give a nonroutine complete quantitative classification. The analysis distinguishes symmetric rotated-saddle geometry from companion-form mechanical counterexamples and isolates practical robustness to duty timing. It is not presented as a general Floquet or Araki inequality, which are existing knowledge.
